problem:
Aster Leisure Group runs monthly gym memberships collected by SEPA Direct Debit. Its support team keeps using the words cancellation and revocation as if they meant the same thing, and the confusion has real consequences. A member who cancels a membership expects no further collection, a billing clerk who revokes a collection expects it never to leave the building, and a creditor PSP that receives a cancellation request expects a scheme message with a response. When the team picks the wrong mechanism for the collection state, the member is debited anyway or the bank rejects the request, and the complaint lands with the same team that chose the wrong word.

The distinction turns on three facts: who initiates the action, what state the collection is in, and which channel carries it. Revocation is a creditor-side action taken while the collection is still within the creditor's control, before submission. A request for cancellation is a scheme action taken after submission, carried by camt.056 with a camt.029 response, and it can be accepted or rejected. A debtor refund is a third thing entirely, initiated by the debtor through the debtor PSP after the collection, and it follows refund rights rather than cancellation logic.

Aster Leisure Group needs a single page its support and billing teams can use without guessing: for each collection state, the correct mechanism, the correct initiator, the correct message, and the correct customer wording.
solution:
Build the decision around a state table that the team consults before acting. State one, collection created but not submitted: the initiator is the creditor, the mechanism is revocation, the channel is the creditor's own collection service or file, and the outcome is immediate exclusion from the submission set with an audit record. No scheme message is sent and no counterparty response is needed.

State two, collection submitted but not settled: the initiator is the creditor through the creditor PSP, the mechanism is a request for cancellation, the channel is camt.056, and the outcome depends on the camt.029 response. The team records the request, waits for the response, and tells the customer the collection is cancelled only after acceptance. If the request is rejected or the original settles first, the team moves to the reversal or refund branch.

State three, collection settled: neither revocation nor cancellation applies. The creditor remedy is a reversal where the scheme permits it, and the debtor remedy is a refund claim under the Core or B2B rules. The team must also distinguish a membership cancellation from a collection cancellation: ending a membership stops future collections by cancelling or ending the mandate, while stopping a single collection that is already in flight needs the mechanism above. Both actions should be recorded so a cancelled member is never collected again in a later billing run.

decision.question: A member cancels their Aster Leisure membership on Monday. The next monthly collection is in the pain.008 file that has been generated but not yet submitted to the creditor PSP. A second member cancelled last month, but their collection was already submitted yesterday for a due date in three days. The learner must choose the correct mechanism for each member.

options.label: A
options.detail: Revoke the first member's collection from the file, and send a camt.056 request for cancellation for the second member.

options.label: B
options.detail: Revoke both collections from the local file and assume both are stopped.

options.label: C
options.detail: Tell both members to claim a refund from their own banks after the collections settle.

options.label: D
options.detail: Send a camt.056 for both members.

decisionRationale: Option A is correct because the mechanism follows the collection state: revocation while still in creditor control, and a scheme cancellation request after submission. Option D is wrong because a camt.056 is not the mechanism for an unsubmitted collection. Option B is wrong because revoking a local copy does not cancel a submitted instruction. Option C is wrong because a refund claim is a post-settlement debtor remedy, not a way to stop a collection that can still be cancelled.

steps.title: Cancels membership through the app or by phone, giving the effective date.
Locates the next collection and checks its state: created, submitted or settled.
For a created but unsubmitted collection, revokes it from the file and marks it revoked with reason and actor.
For a submitted collection, sends a camt.056 request for cancellation with the original instruction reference.
Evaluates the request and returns a camt.029 acceptance or rejection.
Records the camt.029 outcome against the original collection and updates its state.
Notifies the member of the outcome using wording that matches the actual state, and confirms no further collections will be raised.
Ends or cancels the mandate for future periods so the member is not collected again.

happy: Both members are handled by state. The first member's unsubmitted collection is revoked from the file before submission, so no instruction ever leaves the creditor. The second member's submitted collection is stopped by an accepted camt.056, confirmed by a camt.029, before settlement. Both members receive accurate confirmation, their mandates are ended so no future collection is raised, and the audit trail shows the revocation, the request, the acceptance and the mandate end as separate linked events.

negative.title: Revocation attempted after submission
negative.detail: A clerk tries to revoke a collection from the local file after it has already been submitted. Detect the state mismatch from the collection record, block the local revocation, and route the item to the camt.056 cancellation path with an explanation to the clerk.

negative.title: Cancellation request rejected
negative.detail: The counterparty PSP rejects the camt.056 because the collection has passed the cancellable point. Record the camt.029 rejection, tell the member the collection could not be stopped, and prepare a reversal or refund with a clear date.

negative.title: Membership cancelled but mandate left live
negative.detail: The collection is stopped for one month but the mandate remains active, so the next billing run collects again. Treat mandate end as a mandatory step in the membership cancellation checklist, and add a control that flags any collection raised against an ended membership before file generation.

negative.title: Batch booking hides a single-item outcome
negative.detail: A batch posts as one aggregate entry, so a single cancelled collection inside it is hard to trace. Retain item-level references linked to the aggregate posting, so each collection, revocation and cancellation can be reconciled individually against the batch total.

technical: Store the collection state as an explicit field with allowed transitions, and enforce the mechanism by state in the application so a revocation cannot be recorded for a submitted collection and a camt.056 cannot be created for an unsubmitted one. Keep the revocation, the cancellation request and the camt.029 response as separate records linked by the original instruction ID, each with its own ID, actor, timestamp and reason. Make the camt.056 idempotent on its request ID. Link the mandate end to the membership cancellation so future billing runs exclude the member automatically, and validate that linkage before every file generation. For batch booking, keep the aggregate ledger entry linked to its item-level records with control totals, so a single-item return or cancellation reconciles without reversing the successful items in the batch.

messages.title: Collection instruction before submission, revocable by the creditor while still in creditor control.
Request for cancellation of a submitted instruction.

fields.tag: Original instruction ID and End-to-End ID
fields.name: Original instruction ID and End-to-End ID

messages.title: Resolution of investigation, reporting acceptance or rejection of the cancellation request.
Return or reversal where a settled collection must be corrected.

accounting: A revoked collection never enters the in-transit control account, so the billing total and the file total reconcile with the revocation listed as an exclusion. An accepted cancellation clears the expected in-transit entry without a settlement posting, using the camt.029 as clearing evidence. A rejected cancellation that settles posts normally and is then corrected by a linked reversal entry, so the original settlement record stays intact. Where a batch is booked as one aggregate entry, the item-level records carry the individual outcomes and the aggregate reconciles to the sum of its items, including the cancelled and reversed ones. Operations reviews a daily queue of state mismatches, rejected cancellations and mandates left live after membership cancellation, with an SLA that clears each item before the next billing run.

scenarios.given: a collection that has not yet been submitted to the PSP
scenarios.then: it is excluded from submission and marked revoked. no scheme cancellation message is sent for it

scenarios.given: a collection that has been submitted but not yet settled
scenarios.when: a valid cancellation request is accepted
scenarios.then: the original collection follows the scheme cancellation outcome. the member is notified only after the acceptance is recorded

questions.question: Who initiates a revocation, and when is it available?
options: The debtor, before the due date
The clearing mechanism, at any time
The creditor, while the collection is still within creditor control before submission
questions.explanation: Revocation is a creditor-side action available while the collection has not yet been submitted.

questions.question: What message carries a request for cancellation after submission?
questions.explanation: The camt.056 carries the request for cancellation, and the camt.029 reports acceptance or rejection.

questions.question: A cancellation request has been sent. What should the team tell the customer?
options: That the collection is cancelled, immediately
That a refund is on its way
That a cancellation has been requested and the outcome will be confirmed once the response arrives
Nothing until the next billing run
questions.explanation: The request itself does not stop settlement, so the customer must be told the outcome only after the acceptance is recorded.

questions.question: A member cancels their membership. What else must happen to prevent future collections?
options: The creditor PSP must be told verbally
The next collection must be revoked each month
The mandate must be ended or cancelled so later billing runs exclude the member
Nothing, the membership system handles it
questions.explanation: Ending the mandate is the control that stops future collections. Without it, the next billing run can collect again.
